text:
Maya: Hey — running into weirdness when consuming the JS SDK in a mixed ESM/CJS codebase + edge worker. Docs only show `import` examples and it's not clear what to do for older Node apps that still use `require`.

Devon: Can you paste the exact error? usually it's either `...default` being undefined or TS typing issues.

Maya: Repro: app is Node 14 runtime (CJS), worker is edge (V8 ESM). When I do:
```js
// server (CJS)
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
console.log(Redwood); // prints { default: [Function: Client] }
const client = Redwood.createClient(); // TypeError: Redwood.createClient is not a function
```
But in the edge function using `import` it works fine. TS complains in the CJS file unless I enable `esModuleInterop`.

Alex: Yeah this is classic interop. TL;DR: shipping an ESM build with a default export means `require()` consumers see a `{ default: ... }` wrapper unless you also set `module.exports = exports.default` or ship a CJS build. Two practical fixes:
- Prefer ESM `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` in edge and modern Node.
- For CJS, either require the `.default` or enable `esModuleInterop` in tsconfig.

Quick examples:
```js
// ESM (edge / modern node)
import Redwood, { createClient } from '@redwood/inference';
const c = createClient({ key: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });

// CJS fallback
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const createClient = Redwood.createClient || Redwood.default?.createClient;
const c2 = createClient({ key: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY });
```

Sam: I ran into the same with Vercel Edge — it threw `SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module` when bundler config was wrong. For edge you must use ESM bundle and the file extension / package type matters.

Maya: Thanks — that helps. Two follow-ups: (1) Can we get a tiny doc snippet for both CJS and ESM? (2) Any guidance for TypeScript config (esModuleInterop + allowSyntheticDefaultImports)?

Devon: For TS, recommend `{"esModuleInterop": true, "allowSyntheticDefaultImports": true}` in tsconfig if you're a CJS consumer. But callout: that changes how imports compile, so we should show both approaches.

Alex: Agreed. Also note: if you bundle (webpack/rollup/tsup) you can force interop at bundle time — we should mention bundlers. And for runtime-only CJS apps, simplest is `const createClient = require('@redwood/inference').default?.createClient || require('@redwood/inference').createClient`. Ugly but explicit.

Maya: I'll add a short snippet to the sample-app repo to show both patterns. Sam — I'll paste the link when done.

Sam: :thumbsup: Also add a tiny note under "Edge runtimes" about using native ESM and that Cloudflare/Vercel expect ESM in edge functions. Saved me a support ticket.

docs-bot: Thanks for the report — I'm going to add a short section to the SDK docs: "Import patterns for ESM and CJS" with the three examples (ESM, CJS fallback, TS-config note). @Maya can you drop the sample-app PR link here when ready?

Maya: Will do. PR incoming in ~30m with code + a one-line sentence for the SDK README.

Alex: If anyone wants, I can propose a small change in the package build: add a `cjs` entry that re-exports the default to make `require()` cleaner. Might be a minor release.

Devon: That would be great. Low friction for users.

Maya: Thanks y'all — this cleared up the mental model.
